sentences.text: Learned counsel for respondents opposed the prayer.
Considering the reasons for delay and duration of delay, IA No.3026/2021 is allowed.
Heard the main appeal on merit.

This miscellaneous appeal under Order 43 Rule 1 of the CPC has been filed feeling aggrieved by the order dated 27.02.2019 in MJC No.659/2017 by 3rd Additional Member of Motor Accident Claim Tribunal, Bhopal whereby the application of the appellant under Section 5 of Limitation Act, 1969 for condonation of delay in filing the application under Order 9 Rule 9 of CPC for setting aside the order of dismissal of claim Case No.70/2017 has been dismissed.

2. The facts in brief are that appellant/applicant filed an application under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 for compensation regarding personal injuries due to motor vehicle accident claim application was registered as Case No.70/2017 before the 3rd Additional Member of Motor Accident Claim Tribunal, Bhopal.
On 03.08.2017, application was dismissed for non- appearance of the appellant.
An application for a restoration of the CC No.70/2017 was filed on 06.12.2017.
Application was registered as MJC No.659/2017.

An application under Section 5 of condonation of delay was also filed and reason for delay was not mentioned that he appeared on 02.08.2017 before the Motor Accident Claim Tribunal, Bhopal could not get the next date of hearing timely and returned to his home and next date tried to know the delay of progress of case

then counsel intimated that on the same day i.e. 03.08.2017, the case is fixed for evidence then he approach the Court but could not succeed to mark his presence due to over crowded and his case was dismissed and later he got ill and after recovery he filed the application in support of his application he filed affidavit and certificate of Hindustan Hospital, Bhopal regarding illness from 28.08.2017 to 04.12.2017.
3. Respondent Nos.1 and 2 contested the application on the ground that reason for delay does not constituted sufficient ground and concerned certificate is false.
4. Trial Court dismissed the application mainly on the ground that applicant has not explained the delay between 03.08.2017 to 28.08.2017.
Application of the appellant is not bona fide, so the delay of three months cannot be condoned.

5. Heard.
6.
Counsel for the respondents have opposed the prayer and supported the order of trial Court.

7. Perused the record.
8.
Trial Court has not recorded any finding that certificate of illness is not genuine.
Only ground that appellant was not ill during 03.08.2017 to 28.08.2017 is not sound.
Considering the nature of proceeding, the delay is condoned.
